headline: Bronx breaks ground on 229 affordable senior homes at Morris Houses
dek: Sol on Park will reserve 80 homes for current NYCHA residents, set aside 69 for formerly homeless seniors and offer 79 more through the Housing Connect lottery.
body: New York City officials and the New York City Housing Authority broke ground Tuesday on Sol on Park, a 229-apartment, fully affordable senior housing development at the Morris Houses campus in the Bronx.

The project uses the city's Transfer of Assistance program to build on public land while creating new housing for current NYCHA residents, formerly homeless New Yorkers and other low-income seniors. The Mayor's Office described it as the largest use of the program in New York City to date.

The apartment breakdown includes 80 homes reserved for seniors living at Morris I and II, 69 homes for formerly homeless seniors and 79 homes that will be offered through the Housing Connect lottery to low- and middle-income seniors.

The 18-story development is planned to include more than 8,000 square feet of community space, a pedestrian plaza and a new accessible space for the Morris Houses Resident Association. The city also says the building will include health-focused amenities and on-site services tied to Union Community Health Center and Green Bronx Machine's National Health & Wellness Center.

The NRP Group, Selfhelp Realty Group and Foxy Management are developing Sol on Park. Construction is underway, with pre-leasing and early move-ins scheduled for early 2029; the building is designed for LEED Platinum and Passive House standards, according to the Mayor's Office.
location: Morris Houses campus, Bronx, New York
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Bronx breaks ground on 229 affordable senior homes
seoDescription: Sol on Park will bring 229 affordable senior homes to the Morris Houses campus, including units for current NYCHA residents and formerly homeless seniors.
